title: Failing over an API endpoint
summary: A load balancer keeps the API available when a node fails.

steps.n: kubectl connects to the stable load balancer address and not to a single node.
The load balancer sends the request to the first healthy API server.
The node loses power and its API server stops answering health checks.
After a few failed checks the load balancer marks node 1 unhealthy.
The next request from the client arrives at the same endpoint.
The load balancer sends it to node 2, and etcd keeps its quorum with two members.

title: Failure and recovery: a zone is lost
summary: Three nodes in two zones cannot survive losing the larger zone.

steps.n: Two etcd members run in zone A and one in zone B to save cost.
A power event takes down zone A including two of the three members.
The one remaining member cannot reach a majority and refuses writes.
The load balancer finds no API server that can serve write requests.
The operator restores the members in zone A from snapshot after power returns.
Endpoint health shows three healthy members and a leader.
They place one member in each of three zones so one zone can fail safely.

title: Phases of kubeadm init
summary: A control plane is built phase by phase.

steps.n: kubeadm checks the OS, ports, swap and runtime before changing anything.
It creates the cluster CA and the certificates for each component.
It writes static pod manifests for the API server, scheduler, controller manager and etcd.
The kubelet reads the manifests and starts the control plane containers.
kubeadm waits until the API server answers its health check.
It applies CoreDNS and kube-proxy and prints the join command.

title: Failure and recovery: a join that fails
summary: A node cannot join because the token expired.

steps.n: The new node runs the saved join command from a week ago.
The control plane checks the bootstrap token in its token store.
The token expired after twenty four hours, so validation fails.
The node prints that the token is invalid or has expired.
The operator runs token create with print join command on a control plane node.
The new node joins with the fresh command and a fresh CA hash.
The node shows Ready after the network plugin starts on it.

title: Renewing certificates
summary: Renew before expiry and restart the components.

steps.n: A thirty day alert reports the API server certificate expires next month.
kubeadm shows each certificate and its remaining time.
They run certs renew all on each control plane node.
The static pods are restarted so they load the new files.
The API server presents the renewed certificate.
They copy the new admin kubeconfig and confirm kubectl works.

title: Failure and recovery: expired certificates
summary: The cluster stops answering and the fix uses kubeadm on the node.

steps.n: Every command reports that the certificate has expired.
The API server certificate is past its date, so TLS fails before authentication.
The operator signs in to a control plane node by SSH.
kubeadm certs check-expiration lists several certificates as invalid.
certs renew all creates new certificates for all components.
The kubelet restarts the control plane pods which load the new certificates.
kubectl works with the new admin kubeconfig and an expiry alert is added.

title: Upgrading one node
summary: Control plane first, then each worker in turn.

steps.n: kubeadm upgrade plan shows the target and apply moves the first control plane node to it.
On a worker, the operator cordons and drains it so pods move elsewhere.
The scheduler places the evicted pods on other nodes with free capacity.
kubeadm upgrade node and the kubelet package update the worker to the new version.
The kubelet restarts on the new version and reports to the API server.
The node is marked schedulable again and the next worker begins.

title: Failure and recovery: a removed API
summary: An upgrade breaks a deployment that used a removed API version.

steps.n: A pipeline applies a manifest that still uses a deprecated API version.
The cluster is upgraded and that API version no longer exists.
The API server returns no matches for the kind in that version and the pipeline fails.
The operator runs an API deprecation scanner on all manifests and charts.
It lists nine manifests that use removed versions and the replacement for each.
The team updates the versions and fixes the pipeline.
The scan becomes a required step before every upgrade plan.

title: Replacing a node
summary: Add first, drain second, delete last.

steps.n: The operator joins a new node so capacity is higher before anything leaves.
No new pods will land on it while it is being retired.
Pods are evicted gracefully and recreated on other nodes.
The evicted pods start on the new node and pass readiness checks.
The old node is removed from the cluster after it is empty.
The old machine is shut down and its address is released.

title: Restoring etcd from a snapshot
summary: A snapshot becomes a working control plane.

steps.n: The operator picks the newest verified snapshot from the off-node store.
etcdctl snapshot restore writes the data into a fresh data directory.
The etcd static pod manifest is changed to use the new data directory.
The kubelet recreates etcd and the API server connects to the restored data.
Nodes and workloads appear as they were at the time of the snapshot.
Resources created after the snapshot are recreated from source control.

title: Failure and recovery: the snapshot is eight months old
summary: A silent backup failure is found during a recovery.

steps.n: A node rebuild removes the scheduled snapshot job and nobody notices.
Months later the control plane is lost and the team starts a recovery.
The newest file in storage is eight months old.
The old state is restored and many newer deployments are missing.
The team reapplies manifests from the repository to rebuild what is missing.
The snapshot job is moved into the cluster as a CronJob with monitoring.
They alert on snapshot age and rehearse a restore every quarter.

title: Upgrading through Cluster API
summary: A version edit rolls machines in order.

steps.n: The operator changes the Kubernetes version on the control plane object.
The controller sees that the machines do not match the desired version.
It creates a new machine with the new version first.
The new machine joins and reports healthy to the management cluster.
The controller deletes one old machine after the new one is healthy.
The controller repeats one machine at a time within the rollout limits.
